s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms present for more than 10 years
Lesions localized to the left shin
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Multiple milia in the superficial dermis on histopathologic examination
Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene identified

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene identified, which is a known cause of this condition

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation and multiple milia, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoepidermal separation and milia on histopathologic examination, although less common in this condition

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation, although Kindler Syndrome is a rare condition

shortlist.label: Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical and histopathologic features to Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, and the novel COL7A1 variant could be consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of dermoepidermal separation, milia, and a novel heterozygous missense variant in the COL7A1 gene are characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
rejected.why: Typically presents with more generalized skin involvement and is associated with mutations in KRT5 or KRT14 genes

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: Usually presents with more severe and widespread skin and mucous membrane involvement, and is associated with mutations in genes such as COL17A1 or LAMA3

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by a more complex phenotype including photosensitivity, and is associated with mutations in the KIND1 gene

rejected.label: Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: The identified variant is heterozygous, suggesting an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance, which is more consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
